Vote 276, Indians of British Columbia: Adjustments of Previous Payments to Columbia Coast Mission for
Hospital Care, etc.


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, August 22, 1924.

SIR, - British Columbia cheque No. 1579 of 1923 - 24 is for the payment of $797.15 to the Columbia Coast Mission,
Inc., for unpaid Indian Accounts incurred prior to January 1, 1923. This amount is made up as follows: -

Accounts of 1918 - 19       70.00
Accounts of 1919 - 20       267.75
Accounts of 1920 - 21       324.55
Accounts of 1921 - 22      172.75
Accounts of 1922 - 23      70.10
...                        $905.15
Less for 183 hospital days 183.00
...                        $722.15
Doctor's services          75.00
Total                      $797.15

I find that during the period covered by this account the following payments were made by you to the Columbia Coast
Mission: -

Year      Grant for Doctor Treatment
1918 - 19 $600.00          $436.00
1919 - 20 600.00           483.25
1920 - 21 724.99           729.00
1921 - 22 850.00           327.00
1922 - 23 850.00           403.00

In view of the fact that payments were made each year, both for medical services and for hospital treatment, I have to
ask for an explanation of the payment in question. As this institution was in receipt of an annual allowance for medical



=== EXTRACT FROM HERE (pages 557-560) ===
<!-- page 557 -->
services a special explanation of the charge of $75.00 for doctor's services is requested.

<!-- page 558 -->
The account in support of this payment is certified by Mr. W.E. Ditchburn, Chief Inspector of Indian Agencies, from
which I infer that he investigated the circumstances under which this account was presented. If such, is the case I shall
be glad to have a copy of any report that he may have made.


I am, Sir, your obedient servant,
G. GONTHIER, A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, August 25, 1924.

SIR, - Referring to your letter of the 22nd instant, regarding a payment of $797.15 made to the Columbia Coast
Mission by official cheque No. 1579 of 1923 - 24, I beg to transmit as requested by you copy of report dated the
22nd August, 1923, made in this matter by Mr. W.E. Ditchburn who investigated the circumstances under which the
account was presented.


Your obedient servant,
J.D. MCLEAN, Asst. Deputy and Sec'y.


The Auditor General.


INDIAN AGENCIES OFFICE, Victoria, B.C., August 22, 1923.

SIR, - Replying to your letter of the 11th April last, referring to the request of the Columbia Coast Mission for
payment of uncollectible accounts owing by Indians for medical services and hospital treatment at St. George's
Hospital, Alert Bay, amounting to $915.15, I beg to say that in this total will be found $57 for the year 1918, and
$24.75 for 1919 (end of March, 1920), a total of $81.75. These represent accounts which it was thought at the time the
Indians would be able to pay but they have not done so. This leaves a balance of $823.40 for the years 1920-21 and up
to the end of December, 1922, being $445 for 1920, $297.30 for the year 1921 and $81.10 up. to December 31st, 1922.

After making a full investigation into each of these cases it is considered that the hospital will be unable to collect
anything from the Indians and I therefore feel that the Department should pay the accounts. I find, however, that in a
number of cases the Department has already paid certain sums by way of the per them rate of $1 as hospital fees,
being: Jim Adams, 2 days; Mrs. J. Humchit, 62 days; Mrs. Kitty Edwards, 4 days; Mrs. Mollie Hall, 49 days; Tommy
Moon, 20 days, and Louie Williams, 46 days, amounting to $183 which should be deducted from the amount asked,
bringing the total to $722.15.

I took this point up with Mr. Blarton, the secretary of the Columbia Coast Mission, recently, but while admitting that
this amount has already been paid, he takes the stand that if this deduction is to be made certain additions amounting
to $75 for doctor's services, should be allowed in view of the fact that only low charges in this regard had been made
when submitting the accounts to the Indians. This point is worthy of consideration and therefore I am providing for the
amount on the voucher. A copy of Mr. Barton's letter is hereto attached for your information.

In connection with your criticism of the financial statement-rendered by the secretary of the hospital, particularly the
item of cash received for 1920, being $1,943.80, whereas the total value of the work performed for that year

<!-- page 559 -->
was $1,677, I beg to say that Mr. Barton informed me that the difference between these two amounts represents the
collection of some old accounts.

Attached hereto, will be found Voucher No. 26A made up as hereunder: -

Account rendered                          $905 15
Less 183 hospital days at $1 already paid 183 00
...                                       $722 15
Plus doctor's services                    75 00
Total                                     $797 15

I would advise the remittance of this amount at as early a date as possible owing to the fact that the hospital was
burned down a few days ago.


Yours sincerely,
W.E. DITCHBURN, Chief Inspector.


The Auditor General.


COLUMBIA COAST MISSION, VANCOUVER, July 17, 1923.

DEAR MR. DITCHBURN, - Pursuant to our conversation re application for payment from the Department of the
accounts unpaid by indigent Indians, I would like to say that, whereas I do not think with you that the Department
should deduct the per them grant from those accounts which received the same in the list submitted, and which they
have not done hitherto; if they should take that view I would also then submit that the accounts as noted hereunder
should be allowed the usual hospital rate of $2.50 per day, which was not charged in these cases. Of course, in making
the charges, we did not anticipate a return of the per diem grant, and, whatever may have been the reason in these
cases I know the doctor has made reductions in the charges to meet the financial needs of the Indian in hopes he would
pay himself.

Mrs. J. Humsida in hospital Feb. 8 to April 10th, 1920, for 62 days, charged 126 00
(Doctor's fees being only $4.50) at $2.50                                    155 00
...                                                                          $29 00 to add.
Mrs. Mildred Hall in hospital Feb. 8th to Mar. 29, 1920, for 50 days charged $102 00
(Doctor's fees being only $2) at $2.50                                       125 00
...                                                                          $23 00 to add.
Louis Williams in hospital Jan. 4th to Feb. 19th, 1920, for 46 days charged $92 00
(Doctor's fees being only $15.50) at $2.50                                   115 00
...                                                                          $23 00 to add.

These three accounts would total $75 to add.

I would further note that in the account of Alf. A. Thompson, who was in hospital from Nov. 13th to April 7th, 1921,
for 146 days, and for which a charge of hospital fees is made at the usual $2.50 per day the doctor's fee is only
